arxiv-2109-05533.title: Randomized-gauge test for machine learning of Ising model order parameter
arxiv-2109-05533.creator: Tomoyuki Morishita, Synge Todo
arxiv-2109-05533.description: Abstract Recently, machine learning has been applied successfully for identifying phases and phase transitions of the Ising models. The continuous phase transition is characterized by spontaneous symmetry breaking, which can not be detected in general from a single spin configuration.

arxiv-2209-14279.title: Causal Proxy Models for Concept-based Model Explanations
arxiv-2209-14279.creator: Zhengxuan Wu, Karel D’Oosterlink, Atticus Geiger, Amir Zur, Christopher Potts wuzhengx@cs.stanford.edu , karel.doosterlinck@ugent.be , atticusg@stanford.edu , amirzur@stanford.edu , cgpotts@stanford.edu
arxiv-2209-14279.description: Abstract Explainability methods for NLP systems encounter a version of the fundamental problem of causal inference: for a given ground-truth input text, we never truly observe the counterfactual texts necessary for isolating the causal effects of model representations on outputs. In response, many explainability methods make no use of counterfactual texts, assuming they will be unavailable.

arxiv-2402-16654.title: GigaPevt: Multimodal Medical Assistant
arxiv-2402-16654.creator: Pavel Blinov, Konstantin Egorov, Ivan Sviridov, Nikolay Ivanov, Stepan Botman, Evgeniy Tagin, Stepan Kudin, Galina Zubkova, Andrey Savchenko
arxiv-2402-16654.description: Abstract Building an intelligent and efficient medical assistant is still a challenging AI problem. The major limitation comes from the data modality scarceness, which reduces comprehensive patient perception. This demo paper presents the GigaPevt, the first multimodal medical assistant that combines the dialog capabilities of large language models with specialized medical models.

arxiv-2405-05705.title: Detecting Statements in Text: A Domain-Agnostic Few-Shot Solution
arxiv-2405-05705.creator: Sandrine Chausson, Björn Ross
arxiv-2405-05705.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sandrine Chausson, Björn Ross. Many tasks related to Computational Social Science and Web Content Analysis involve classifying pieces of text based on the claims they contain. State-of-the-art approaches usually involve fine-tuning models on large annotated datasets, which are costly to produce. In light of this, we propose and release a qualitative and versatile few-shot learning methodology as a common paradigm for any claim-based textual classification task.

arxiv-2510-20909.title: Code-enabled language models can outperform reasoning models on diverse tasks
arxiv-2510-20909.creator: Cedegao E. Zhang, Cédric Colas, Gabriel Poesia, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Jacob Andreas
arxiv-2510-20909.description: Abstract Reasoning models (RMs), language models (LMs) trained with reinforcement learning to produce long-form natural language reasoning, have been remarkably successful, but they still require large amounts of computation and data to train, and can be slow and expensive to run.

arxiv-2601-02654.title: Thermalized buckling of extensible, semiflexible polymers
arxiv-2601-02654.creator: Richard Huang, David R. Nelson, Suraj Shankar
arxiv-2601-02654.description: Abstract The Euler buckling of rods is a long-studied mechanical instability, and it remains relevant to this day, as the constituent components in many biological and physical systems are linear polymers, such as microtubules or carbon nanotubes. At finite temperature, if a polymer is shorter than its persistence length, the polymer is semiflexible, and its elasticity remains rod-like.

arxiv-2602-20929.title: Fair Division with Soft Conflicts
arxiv-2602-20929.creator: Hirotaka Yoneda, Masataka Yoneda
arxiv-2602-20929.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Hirotaka Yoneda, Masataka Yoneda. We study the fair division of indivisible goods with conflicts between pairs of goods, represented by a graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) . We consider “soft” conflicts: assigning two adjacent goods to the same agent is allowed, but we seek allocations that are envy-free up to one good (EF1) while keeping the number of such conflict violations small.

pmc-10492371.title: Sustainable production of photosynthetic isobutanol and 3-methyl-1-butanol in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
pmc-10492371.creator: Hao Xie, Jarl Kjellström, Peter Lindblad
pmc-10492371.description: BackgroundCyanobacteria are emerging as green cell factories for sustainable biofuel and chemical production, due to their photosynthetic ability to use solar energy, carbon dioxide and water in a direct process. The model cyanobacterial strain Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 has been engineered for the isobutanol and 3-methyl-1-butanol production by introducing a synthetic 2-keto acid pathway.

pmc-10693600.title: Colliding heavy nuclei take multiple identities on the path to fusion
pmc-10693600.creator: Kaitlin J Cook, Dominic C Rafferty, David J Hinde, Edward C Simpson, Mahananda Dasgupta, Lorenzo Corradi, Maurits Evers, Enrico Fioretto, Dongyun Jeung, Nikolai Lobanov, Duc Huy Luong, Tea Mijatović, Giovanna Montagnoli, Alberto M Stefanini, Suzana Szilner
pmc-10693600.description: The properties of superheavy elements probe extremes of physics and chemistry. They are synthesised at accelerator laboratories using nuclear fusion, where two atomic nuclei collide, stick together (capture), then with low probability evolve to a compact superheavy nucleus. The fundamental microscopic mechanisms controlling fusion are not fully understood, limiting predictive capability.

pmc-12603863.title: Analysis of risk factors for kidney stones in patients with hyperuricemia: a cross-sectional study based on NHANES
pmc-12603863.creator: Xiaojing Liu, Jingjing Zhou, Conghui Liu, Feng Shao, Zhongxin Li
pmc-12603863.description: BackgroundHyperuricemia is a growing public health concern and a well-established risk factor for nephrolithiasis. However, the specific interplay of demographic, clinical, and biochemical factors that contribute to kidney stone formation within this high-risk population is not fully elucidated, particularly in a large, nationally representative cohort.

pmc-12676324.title: Mitigation of the Anodic Shift of the Onset Potential in a TiO2/α-Fe2O3 Photoanode by Inserting a Nickel Ferrite (NiFe2O4) Blocking Layer
pmc-12676324.creator: Seong Kyu Jang, Seung Hyeon Jeong, Aram Hong, Woon Yong Sohn
pmc-12676324.description: It is widely recognized that the insertion of TiO2 as a blocking layer into a photoanode in a PEC (photoelectrochemical) system can retard the electron–hole back recombination. However, it has been also reported that it can induce an anodic shift in the onset potential in the current density–voltage curve.

pmc-12718190.title: VRK1 co-delivery mitigates DNA clustering by BAF in TFAMoplex transfection
pmc-12718190.creator: Christina Greitens, Philip Maurer, Selen Balkan, Jean-Christophe Leroux, Michael Burger
pmc-12718190.description: In non-viral gene delivery, DNA entering the cytoplasm is rapidly bound by barrier-to-autointegration factor (BAF) and surrounded by nuclear envelope-like membranes. This process is thought to mitigate the translocation of the DNA from the cytoplasm through the nuclear pores limiting the transfection of interphase cells.

pmc-12738079.title: Station Holding During Rheotaxis: A Sensitive Assay of Lateral Line Function in Larval Zebrafish
pmc-12738079.creator: Sophie Cohen-Bodénès, Elayna I. Malak, Josef G. Trapani, Matt Gaidica, Valentin A. Militchin, Kyle C. Newton, Lavinia Sheets
pmc-12738079.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Hair cells are the sensory receptors of the auditory and vestibular systems in the inner ears of all vertebrates. Hair cells also serve to detect water flow in the lateral line system in amphibians and fish. The zebrafish lateral line serves as a well-established model for investigating hair cell development and function, including research on genetic mutations associated with deafness and environmental factors that cause hair cell damage.

pmc-13279193.title: Dissection of MAPK and NF-κB p65 signaling dynamics underlying LPS tolerance in macrophages at the single-cell level
pmc-13279193.creator: Tuntikorn Laosuk, Patipark Kueanjinda, Hiroshi Kimura, Tanapat Palaga
pmc-13279193.description: Highlights•Single-cell imaging reveals changed signaling pattern in LPS tolerance.•LPS tolerance delays the kinetic of first NF-κB and ERK activation.•Inhibition studies reveal bidirectional crosstalk between NF-κB and ERK dynamics.Keywords: LPS tolerance, Macrophages, ERK, NF-κB, Signaling dynamics Introduction The innate immune system is the first line defense mechanism against infections [1].

pmc-13397169.title: Speciation of European bullheads ( Cottus spp.): The next problem for taxonomy of northern freshwater fishes
pmc-13397169.creator: David S. Murray, Vladimír Kováč, David Wright, Gordon H. Copp
pmc-13397169.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). High morphological and ecological diversity displayed by European bullheads led Freyhof et al. (2005) to describe 15 nominal species. However, the basis for declaring these nominal species is contentious due to a lack of rigorous statistical analysis of morphological variations among populations, limitations in the inferences made from previous generations of molecular studies, a dearth of next‐generation sequencing tools for European bullheads and an underestimation of the complexity of evolutionary processes.

pmc-13670626.title: Comparative analysis of laparoscopic internal ring reinforcement combined with high ligation versus double-loop high ligation in the treatment of pediatric giant inguinal hernia
pmc-13670626.creator: Qingbao He, Hongjia He, Kaisheng Li, Xiaoyang Liu
pmc-13670626.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the clinical outcomes of laparoscopic internal ring reinforcement combined with high ligation and double-loop high ligation in the treatment of pediatric giant inguinal hernia.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 381 children with giant inguinal hernia who underwent laparoscopic repair at the Children’s Hospital Affiliated to Shandong University between February 2021 and April 2025.
